examples.en: I wash my hands thoroughly.

examples.ko: 밥을 먹고 나서 그릇을 깨끗이 씻었어요.
examples.en: After eating, I washed the dishes well.
I cleaned the room thoroughly.
I wiped the windows clean.
If the shoes are dirty, please wash them clean.

explain: 깨끗이는 “하나도 안 남기고”라는 느낌이에요. 그래서 “밥을 깨끗이 먹었어요”처럼 음식을 다 먹을 때도 써요.

phrases.en: to admit something frankly, without excuses
phrases.nuance_en: used when you admit something plainly, without making excuses
phrases.en_equiv: to admit something frankly, without excuses

dict_examples.ko: 나는 흐르는 물에 상추를 깨끗이 씻었다.
dict_examples.en: I washed the lettuce clean under running water.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 깨끗이 has the feel of “leaving nothing behind”. So it is also used for finishing a meal completely: 밥을 깨끗이 먹었어요.

examples.en: I brush my teeth before bed.
After lunch I brush my teeth in the office bathroom.
When I get up in the morning, I brush my teeth first.
I brush my teeth and wash my face.
If you don't brush your teeth, they hurt.

explain: “이를 닦다”도 같은 뜻이에요. 대화에서는 “양치(하다)”를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: 이를 닦다 means the same thing. In conversation, 양치(하다) is heard more often.

en: going to work; arriving at work

examples.en: Before work, I exercise in the park.

examples.ko: 월요일 출근 시간에는 지하철이 너무 복잡해요.
examples.en: The subway is packed during the Monday morning commute.
It's my first day at work. I'm very nervous.
Do you work tomorrow? — No, I'm off.
It rained, so I was very late getting to work.

explain: 일하러 갈 때는 “출근하다”라고 해요. 회사뿐 아니라 가게나 병원에 갈 때도 써요. 학교에 가는 것은 “등교”예요.

phrases.example: 저는 그 카페에 매일 출근 도장을 찍어요.
phrases.en: to show up somewhere every day (as if clocking in)
phrases.nuance_en: used when you show up at the same place every day without missing
phrases.en_equiv: to show up somewhere every day (as if clocking in)

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 요즈음은 교통난 때문에 출근이 큰 고역이다.
dict_examples.en: These days, commuting is a real ordeal because of traffic congestion.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 출근은 했지만 방학 중인 학교에는 달리 할 일도 없었다.
dict_examples.en: I went to work, but there was nothing else to do at the school during vacation.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Use 출근하다 whenever you go to work, not only to an office but also to a shop or a hospital. Going to school is 등교.

examples.en: The subway is crowded when people get off work.
Quitting time is usually six o'clock.
Today there's a meeting before I leave work.
I have a lot of work today. I'll leave late.

examples.ko: 우리 회사 직원들은 퇴근 후에 운동해요.
examples.en: People at my company exercise after work.

explain: 퇴근은 출근의 반대말이에요. 퇴근할 때 동료에게 “수고하셨습니다”라고 많이 인사해요.

dict_examples.en: closing time; time to leave work
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그는 일이 밀려 퇴근을 못 하고 있다.
dict_examples.en: He is behind on work and can't leave the office.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 퇴근 is the opposite of 출근. When leaving work, people often greet colleagues with 수고하셨습니다 (“thank you for your hard work”).

examples.en: I check my alarm before going to bed.
I didn't hear my alarm and overslept.
The alarm is ringing. Time to get up.
I turned off the alarm and went back to sleep.

examples.ko: 알람 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The alarm was so loud that it startled me.

examples.ko: 내일 일찍 일어나야 해서 여섯 시에 알람을 맞췄어요.
examples.en: I have to get up early tomorrow, so I set the alarm for six.

explain: 알람(alarm)과 알림(notification)은 달라요. 정한 시간에 울리면 “알람”, 휴대폰에 메시지가 오면 “알림”이에요.

dict_examples.ko: 정오에 맞춘 알람을 듣지 못한 채 엄마는 계속 잠을 청했다.
dict_examples.en: Without hearing the alarm set for noon, Mom kept trying to sleep.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Do not mix up 알람 (an alarm that rings at a set time) and 알림 (a notification, such as a message on your phone).

examples.en: What do we need to bring for class tomorrow?
I packed everything I need for the hike.
What to bring on the picnic is a lunch box and water.

examples.ko: 오늘 준비물이 있어요? — 네, 공책하고 펜이 필요해요.
examples.en: Do I need to bring anything today? — Yes, you need a notebook and a pen.
I write the list of things to bring on paper and put it in my bag.

explain: 준비물은 준비(preparation)와 물(物, thing)이 합쳐진 말이에요. “가지고 오세요”라는 안내 밑에 목록 제목으로 많이 써요.

dict_examples.en: things to prepare for a trip
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 내일 학교에 가져갈 미술 준비물을 가방에 넣었다.
dict_examples.en: I put the art supplies to take to school tomorrow in my bag.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 준비물 is 준비 (preparation) + 물 (物, thing). You often see it as the title of a list under a notice that says “please bring these”.

examples.en: Check the order of the moves before you exercise.
I stood in line and waited my turn.
Please sit in order of your names.
If you don't know the order of the cooking steps, look at the book.
It's my turn. Just a moment.

explain: 비슷한 말은 “차례”예요. 게임이나 줄에서 “제 차례예요”라고 많이 말해요.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역
국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to arrange in the correct order
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to line up in order of height
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: A similar word is 차례. In games and in lines, people often say 제 차례예요 (“It's my turn”).

dis.h: everyday word; order in a line or list

p.n: The other word means steps of a procedure, so it is unnatural for list order.
